Threshold-Schooled.effect: While actively holding a threshold, hostile NPCs spend an additional Action to cross it. Costs your React for the scene.

Ward-Literate.summary: You can read active wards, recognize their purpose, and assist with ward work.
Ward-Literate.access: Ghost, Ember Court Old Tie, or extended Shade contact
Ward-Literate.effect: Automatically detect a ward and its category. Navigating around it is Routine. You cannot disarm it.

Illusion-Touched.summary: You have limited access to minor illusion practice without being a full Shade.
Illusion-Touched.access: Tangle-Born, Tidecrew, or goblin hedge-magic contact
Illusion-Touched.effect: Once per scene as a free action, create brief unstable visual illusions: copies, a distraction, or a false position.

Resonant.summary: You can feel local magical resonance and when the layer is unusually active.
Resonant.access: Signal, Radio Sewers contact, or extended signal-layer exposure
Resonant.effect: Once per session after Perform or Broadcast, the GM may declare it Resonant. It is treated as genuinely true and alerts magically sensitive entities in the district.

startingLoadouts.Wrench: Tool kit (professional), light weapon, work clothes, medkit (basic), 200 credits
startingLoadouts.Striker: Standard weapon, light weapon, medium armor, 150 credits
startingLoadouts.Ghost: Light weapon x2, concealment gear, forgery kit (basic), 250 credits
startingLoadouts.Signal: Recording device, broadcast kit (portable), light weapon, 200 credits
startingLoadouts.Shade: Ritual materials (basic), light weapon, ward components, 175 credits
startingLoadouts.Broker: Light weapon, professional clothes, encrypted comm device, 300 credits
startingLoadouts.Warden: Standard weapon, medium armor, civic credentials, restraints, 150 credits
startingLoadouts.Runner: Light weapon, climbing kit, city map (annotated), courier bag, 225 credits

shadeWorkings.name: Sense the Layer
shadeWorkings.desc: Sense active magic and its family in a location, object, or person for one scene.
shadeWorkings.channel: Sense both the magical present and magical past.

shadeWorkings.name: Echo Reading
shadeWorkings.desc: Learn the dominant emotion and one true fact about the most significant event in a space.
shadeWorkings.channel: Receive three clear facts instead of one.
shadeWorkings.res: Death Worker in a death-echo location: automatic and free.

shadeWorkings.name: Disrupt
shadeWorkings.desc: Suppress active magic in a zone for the scene; partial success suppresses it for one round.
shadeWorkings.channel: Break the working permanently instead of suppressing it.

shadeWorkings.name: Hex
shadeWorkings.desc: Place one defined curse: -1 die to a category, force a partial result on a specific next roll, or deny cover against you.
shadeWorkings.channel: Applies to all rolls and lasts until Disrupted.

shadeWorkings.name: Still the Room
shadeWorkings.desc: Project wrongness into a zone; failed Root checks force retreat or penalties.
shadeWorkings.channel: Expand to a building floor or exterior block for the scene.
shadeWorkings.res: At Resonance 1+, increase the Root-check difficulty one tier.

shadeWorkings.name: Mend the Resonant
shadeWorkings.desc: Clear minor magical disruption, stabilize a degraded magical object, or tidy the edges of a working.
shadeWorkings.channel: Clear all minor disruption in the zone and refresh your active workings.

shadeWorkings.name: Bind the Echo
shadeWorkings.desc: Anchor a death echo to a location for one week and create a persistent watched presence.
shadeWorkings.channel: Anchor indefinitely; hostile NPCs begin with 1 Stress.

shadeWorkings.name: Mark the Passage
shadeWorkings.desc: Learn cause of death, final facing, and one unfulfilled final intention.
shadeWorkings.channel: Learn the full hour before death and whether it was witnessed.

shadeWorkings.name: The Pale Hand
shadeWorkings.desc: Target marks 2 Stress and takes -1 die for the scene; injured targets may freeze for one round.
shadeWorkings.channel: Target marks 4 Stress and the penalty lasts until leaving.

shadeWorkings.name: Carry the Dead
shadeWorkings.desc: Carry a death echo for the session, gaining +2 dice when serving its intention and one free Speak to the Dead.
shadeWorkings.channel: Carry two echoes; comfort-based recovery is blocked for the arc.

shadeWorkings.name: Seal the Threshold
shadeWorkings.desc: Hostile creatures must beat your casting successes to cross a sealed threshold.
shadeWorkings.channel: Seal every threshold in a building and raise entry difficulty.

shadeWorkings.name: Alarm
shadeWorkings.desc: Maintain a condition-based magical alarm sensed anywhere in the city.
shadeWorkings.channel: Hide it from magical detection and receive a brief image when triggered.

shadeWorkings.name: Reinforce
shadeWorkings.desc: Make a ward harder to Disrupt or give a physical barrier soak 2 against breach attempts.
shadeWorkings.channel: Reinforce all wards in the location and increase disruption difficulty by two tiers.

shadeWorkings.name: Sanctuary
shadeWorkings.desc: Create a maintained refuge that reduces magical costs, blocks external workings and divine collection, and improves recovery.
shadeWorkings.channel: Double healing and extend cost reduction to all Shades inside.

shadeWorkings.name: Brand
shadeWorkings.desc: Mark a target so later attacks accumulate Stress; reaching a Condition also moves the Wound Track.
shadeWorkings.channel: Apply 2 Stress immediately and make later attacks add 2 Stress.

shadeWorkings.name: Shatter
shadeWorkings.desc: Target loses its next turn, Conditions worsen, and carried workings are suppressed.
shadeWorkings.channel: Lose two turns and worsen Conditions on all enemies who perceive you.

shadeWorkings.name: Curse of Echoes
shadeWorkings.desc: Bind an echo that penalizes attacks and intimidation and causes dramatic hesitation.
shadeWorkings.channel: Penalty applies to all actions and hesitation may trigger twice per scene.

shadeWorkings.name: Burning Account
shadeWorkings.desc: Call every open divine account carried by a target immediately.
shadeWorkings.channel: Reveal and call hidden, denied, forgotten, or inherited accounts.

layLow.name: Lay Low
layLow.desc: Reduce personal Heat by 1, or by 2 when the downtime is spent in your grith.

workContact.name: Work a Contact
workContact.desc: Roll Savvy + Network. On a success or partial success, improve one territory/faction Standing by 1 or prevent a pending Standing loss.

recover.name: Recover
recover.desc: Clear one Condition or move the Wound Track one step toward Unharmed.

putDownRoots.name: Put Down Roots
putDownRoots.desc: Establish grithrakt in the selected district. Requires supporting fiction and is limited by your Root capacity.

settleAccount.name: Settle an Account
settleAccount.desc: Close an open divine Account after its price has been met. The GM confirms the payment; the tool records the closure.

train.name: Train
train.desc: Spend accumulated Marks toward an ability or approved advancement. The tool tracks the Marks and records what was unlocked.

sideJob.name: Side Job
sideJob.desc: Earn GM-approved credits. A Side Job may also generate Heat.

community.name: Community
community.desc: Spend time with someone who matters. Clear 2 Stress, or 3 Stress when this happens in your grith.

research.name: Research
research.desc: Investigate a person, location, or faction. The GM provides one true piece of information; the tool records it.

craft.name: Craft
craft.desc: Wrench only. Build, modify, or prepare equipment for the next job. Record the project and any GM-approved result.

mixedHeritage.summary: Optional, with GM approval. One body, one primary rules package, one inherited echo, and twice as many ways for the city to misread you. The Primary Species gives the full package; the Secondary Heritage gives one Heritage Mark and a required Social Complication, and no stats, abilities, resistances, or vulnerabilities.
mixedHeritage.compatibilityNote: Goblin, Orc, Human, Elf, Dwarf, Halfling and Troll combine freely. Fairy, Kobold, Slimefolk and Cinderfolk ordinarily take Secondary Heritage only from their own lineage; same-lineage or cross-lineage heritage needs GM and canon approval and a custom Heritage Mark.

marks.name: Route Instinct
marks.text: Once per session, in a district you know, ask the GM for one unofficial exit, service door, shortcut, patrol warning, or maintenance gap. Weaker than full Goblin Routes.

marks.name: Small-Space Nerves
marks.text: +1 die once per session when squeezing, hiding, escaping, or acting inside cramped infrastructure.

marks.name: Clan Ear
marks.text: Once per session, recognize whether a rumor, warning, street mark, or local phrase sounds like genuine goblin threnn or outsider noise.

marks.name: Reflex Echo
marks.text: Once per session, when surprised in close quarters, act before a non-elite NPC who did not specifically prepare for you.

marks.name: Chemical Stomach
marks.text: Once per session, ignore a minor bad-air, spoiled-food, weak-chemical, or low-grade contamination effect that would make others hesitate.

marks.name: Demonstrated Weight
marks.text: Once per session, after succeeding at a physical task, gain +1 die on the next related physical task in the same scene.

marks.name: Direct Read
marks.text: Once per session, ask the GM whether a person in front of you is posturing, ready to act, or waiting for someone else to move first.

marks.name: Heavy Frame
marks.text: Once per session, reduce the effect of being shoved, knocked down, moved, or crowded by ordinary force.

marks.name: No Empty Threats
marks.text: Once per session, +1 die on Intimidate or Negotiate when your statement is plain, direct, and backed by something you have already demonstrated.

marks.name: Work Proven
marks.text: Once per session, in an industrial, martial, or labor context, someone takes your competence seriously after you show proof rather than make a claim.

marks.name: Institutional Familiarity
marks.text: Once per session, reduce suspicion in a civic, corporate, or official space where human-coded appearance, paperwork, or speech helps.

marks.name: Paper Trail
marks.text: Once per session, know which office, permit, form, desk, or procedure applies to the current civic problem.

marks.name: Default Face
marks.text: Once per session, in a crowd where humans are common, avoid being treated as unusual unless your other heritage is obvious.

marks.name: Flexible Habit
marks.text: Once per session, +1 die on a skill where you have no rank, if the action is ordinary and not specialized.

marks.name: Civic Memory
marks.text: Once per session, recall a basic institutional rule, social expectation, or legal phrase that helps you avoid immediate trouble.

marks.name: Old Memory
marks.text: Once per session, ask the GM for one old historical, institutional, or magical detail about a place, family, faction, or tradition.

marks.name: Composed Nerves
marks.text: Once per session, ignore a minor panic, morale, or fear effect that relies on surprise rather than real threat.

marks.name: Archive Sense
marks.text: Once per session, know where a formal record, old document, academic source, or long-term witness might exist.

marks.name: Long Courtesy
marks.text: Once per session, +1 die in a formal, academic, old-money, legal, or institutional conversation where etiquette matters.

marks.name: Magical Static
marks.text: Once per session, notice that magic has touched a place, object, or person. Presence, not detail.

marks.name: Material Sense
marks.text: Once per session, identify bad metal, poor repair, structural weakness, hidden stress, or a part about to fail.

marks.name: Built Stubborn
marks.text: Once per session, ignore one minor environmental penalty from cold, bad footing, unstable ground, vibration, or poor working conditions.

marks.name: Good Work Eye
marks.text: Once per session, tell whether something forged, repaired, or built was made properly, cheaply, lovingly, or dangerously.

marks.name: Hold Weight
marks.text: Once per session, +1 die on a task involving carrying, holding, bracing, or keeping something from failing.

marks.name: Stronghold Echo
marks.text: Once per session, in an industrial, workshop, mining, or forge context, recognize who respects real craft and who is pretending.

marks.name: Easy to Miss
marks.text: Once per session, in a crowd or busy public space, avoid casual notice unless you draw attention.

marks.name: Market Ear
marks.text: Once per session, know whether a price, offer, or informal deal sounds fair, dangerous, insulting, or too good to be clean.

marks.name: Soft Step
marks.text: Once per session, move quietly through a busy or cluttered space without triggering casual noise-based attention.

marks.name: Favor Thread
marks.text: Once per session, know someone who knows someone in a trade, market, delivery, or information context. A lead, not a solution.

marks.name: Harmless Read
marks.text: Once per session, benefit from being underestimated as background or not worth immediate attention.

marks.name: Room Current
marks.text: Once per session, sense the dominant emotional tone of a room without identifying individual thoughts or motives.

marks.name: Promise Prickle
marks.text: Once per session, know that someone knowingly broke a promise made in your presence. You learn that the promise was broken, not why.

marks.name: Glamour Echo
marks.text: Once per session, alter one minor sensory detail of your appearance, voice, scent, or clothing for a scene. It cannot change body size, create functional equipment, or perfectly impersonate a known person.

marks.name: Wing Catch
marks.text: Once per session, arrest a fall, clear a short gap, reach a nearby ledge, or descend safely from a modest height. This is not sustained flight.

marks.name: Threshold Instinct
marks.text: Once per session, know whether a nearby doorway, crossing, invitation, or boundary carries supernatural rules, wards, or unusual significance.

Fairy.note: Fairy Heritage Marks are available only to a character with permitted Fae-lineage ancestry. They cannot be used by themselves to create an ordinary mortal/Fairy biological pairing. Gremlin ancestry remains a hybrid-derived Fae heritage and requires a canon-supported origin.

marks.name: Ash Sense
marks.text: Once per session, sense whether violence, death, contract magic, fire, or heat trauma touched a place recently.

marks.name: Heat Familiar
marks.text: Once per session, ignore discomfort from ordinary heat, smoke, ash, warm rooms, or non-damaging flame proximity.

marks.name: Contract Ear
marks.text: Once per session, hear the dangerous part of a deal, promise, or obligation before you sign onto it.

marks.name: Ember Face
marks.text: Once per session, in Ember Court or an occult trade context, be read as belonging enough to avoid immediate outsider treatment.

marks.name: Threshold Itch
marks.text: Once per session, know whether a door, room, shop, or ritual space has rules attached to crossing it.

Cinderfolk.note: Cinderfolk Heritage Marks are available only to a character with permitted Infernal-lineage ancestry. They cannot be used to create a mortal/Cinderfolk or cross-lineage biological pairing.

marks.name: Deep Sense
marks.text: Once per session, sense supernatural wrongness, death pressure, ancestral weight, or spiritual disturbance in broad terms.

marks.name: Heavy Bones
marks.text: Once per session, reduce the effect of a minor fall, shove, collision, or impact that would move or drop you.

marks.name: Old Voice
marks.text: Once per session, +1 die when speaking calmly in a serious moment where presence, grief, memory, or spiritual weight matters.

marks.name: Layered World
marks.text: Once per session, ask whether a place feels spiritually ordinary, disturbed, hungry, watched, dead, or protected.

marks.name: Ancestor Echo
marks.text: Once per session, recall a fragment of family or inherited wisdom relevant to death, obligation, shelter, or warning.

mixedHeritage.customMarkRules:
A custom Mark may: give +1 die once per session in a narrow situation; answer one narrow question once per session; reduce one minor consequence once per session; provide a social opening; create a clue or lead; establish a small inherited trait.

A custom Mark may not: copy a full species passive or active; grant full resistance; erase a vulnerability; add stat modifiers; grant constant armor or Defense; grant free spellcasting, cybernetics, or a class feature; or replace Origin, Life, subclass, or skill investment.

complications.name: Registry Mismatch
complications.text: Your ACR papers, your body, and your community each tell a different story.

complications.name: Read Wrong
complications.text: Strangers guess your species incorrectly and treat you by the mistake.

complications.name: Split Claim
complications.text: Two communities claim you when it's useful and reject you when it isn't.

complications.name: Passing Cost
complications.text: You can pass as one side in some spaces, but it costs trust in others.

complications.name: Family Debt
complications.text: One side expects you to honor traditions the other side never accepted.

complications.name: Corporate Interest
complications.text: Helix, Crownline, Velvet Signal, or another power treats your mixed status as useful data.

complications.name: Civic Confusion
complications.text: ACW or ACR cannot decide which category applies, and the uncertainty turns dangerous.

complications.name: Community Suspicion
complications.text: A community that should accept you tests you harder than anyone else.

complications.name: Too Visible
complications.text: You cannot pass cleanly as either side. Everyone notices, everyone guesses.

complications.name: Too Invisible
complications.text: You pass too well as one side, and people erase the other.

complications.name: Blood Argument
complications.text: People treat your heritage as a debate they may have in front of you.

complications.name: Wrong Tradition
complications.text: You inherited a tradition without being raised in it, or were raised in it without looking the part.

complications.name: Medical Problem
complications.text: Medics, surgeons, and healers do not know which assumptions apply to your body.

complications.name: Standing Drift
complications.text: Your Standing moves differently across communities; a favor in one space damages trust in another.

complications.name: Name Problem
complications.text: Your name, line, clan mark, or appearance tells a story people keep reading wrong.

registrations.name: Clean Primary Registration
registrations.text: ACR lists only the Primary Species; the Secondary is unrecorded or invisible.

registrations.name: Clean Mixed Registration
registrations.text: Records correctly list Mixed Heritage. Rare, and useful.

registrations.name: Outdated Registration
registrations.text: Records use old, hostile, or incomplete terminology.

registrations.name: Corporate Flag
registrations.text: Helix, Crownline, Bastion, or another corporate system holds a separate classification.

registrations.name: Missing Record
registrations.text: The character lives in community memory but not in clean paperwork.

registrations.name: Protected Record
registrations.text: Someone deliberately shielded or altered the record.

registrations.name: Weaponized Record
registrations.text: Someone uses the mixed classification to deny service, access, work, medical care, or protection.

mixedHeritage.subclassRule: Primary Species unlocks racial subclasses. With GM approval, and an Origin and Life that back it, you may take your Secondary Heritage's racial subclass eligibility instead. Never both.

afflictions._source: First Edition v1.47, Chapter Twenty (framework pitched by Ekois). Beastkin is a draft, not yet in the rulebook.
afflictions.summary: Class answers "what do you do?" An Affliction answers "what has the Hidden Layer done to you?" It is not a species and not a profession: something that happened to an already-mortal person. Every Affliction has a Passive, an Active, a Compulsion, a Weakness, and an Evolution. Stage advancement is a GM-adjudicated story event, never a Mark spend.
afflictions.stressRule: As Stress rises, the Active may strengthen, the Compulsion is more likely to assert itself unprompted, and the Weakness becomes easier to exploit.

Vampire.source: Chapter Twenty: Worked Example (first draft, pending playtest)
Vampire.summary: A mortal person of any species carrying a blood-fed magical condition. Blood sustains Vitality, a pool of stolen life force that powers vampiric ability.

resource.name: Vitality
resource.rule: Maximum Vitality = (2 x Wound Track Capacity) + floor(Maximum Magical Veins / 4). Exact per-character totals are confirmed in the post-playtest pass.

passive: Sense living resonance: tell, in general terms, whether a living person is nearby and roughly how many, without a roll.
Arrested aging: stops aging at the point of turning (civic paperwork lists both ages).

adaptation.rule: One permanent +1, flat and additive on top of species. The other two come only through Blood Surge.

active.name: Feed
active.text: Blood refills Vitality. Legal (city-sanctioned supply), corporate contract (commonly Bastion or Helix), or illegal (hunting).

active.name: Blood Surge
active.text: Spend Vitality to briefly push past baseline, including the two Attribute bonuses not taken as the permanent adaptation. Exact costs pending playtest.

compulsion.name: Hunger
compulsion.text: A gradient of remaining Vitality. Stress accelerates the slide; as Stress rises the GM may have Hunger assert itself unprompted.
ladder: Full control; adaptation and Blood Surge work normally
Blood is distracting; Blood Surge visibly intensifies Hunger
-1 die on all checks; the permanent +1 is suspended; Blood Surge still available
Severe Compulsion; Blood Surge only for pursuing blood, escaping, resisting restraint, or preventing defeat this turn
No Vitality abilities and no Attribute enhancement; dormancy, frenzy, or collapse

weakness.name: Sunlight
weakness.text: Direct, sustained exposure moves the Wound Track once per round, no roll, no Defense. Brief or incidental exposure does not trigger it at Dormant or Awakened (GM call). Never softens with Evolution.

complication.name: Registered Vampire
complication.text: Registered and technically protected under ACR, but any vampiric crime in the district puts you under practical presumption of guilt.

progression.Dormant: Resonance sense only; adaptation not online; small Vitality pool. Hunger slides slowly.
progression.Awakened: Permanent +1 online; Blood Surge; Resistance Necrotic. Full Hunger gradient.
progression.Integrated: Longer resonance range, efficient feeding, wider Blood Surge. Hunger intrudes more under Stress. Incidental sunlight imposes a die penalty.
progression.Manifest: A new Vitality-powered Active (scope TBD). Deep Hunger can force a Breakdown-like complication. Sustained sunlight moves the Wound Track two steps per round.
progression.Ascendant: Capstone Vitality abilities. GM may direct one action per scene under high Stress or deep Hunger. Any direct sunlight moves the Wound Track.

Beastkin.source: Draft by Eko with Nib's go-ahead, built on the Chapter Twenty framework and kept to the World Anvil (Supernatural Lineage, Fae, Visceral, Corporations, Biotech Retrieval Units). Not in the First Edition rulebook yet.
Beastkin.summary: An Affliction, so it is something that happened to a person who already existed: your species, family and lineage stay yours. Beastkin carry an animal Aspect because an ancestor was cursed, Fae-touched, experimented on, or contaminated, and it surfaces in them. Lycan is the best-known line. Your bloodline decides your Bane.

aspects.name: Hunter
aspects.text: Wolf, big cat, hound. Chase, pin, finish.

aspects.name: Prey
aspects.text: Hare, deer, rat. Notice first, run first, survive.

aspects.name: Pack
aspects.text: Dog, hyena, crow. Strength is the group.

aspects.name: Den
aspects.text: Bear, badger, boar. Hold ground, endure, protect the burrow.

resource.name: The Beast
resource.rule: No separate pool. The Beast routes through Stress, as the framework intends: the higher your Stress, the closer it is to the surface.

passive: Animal senses: scent, hearing, or low-light sight (by Aspect). Without a roll, tell whether fear, blood, or a predator is present in the scene, in general terms.
Pack read: once per scene, know who in the room would fight, flee, or follow if it went bad.

adaptation.rule: One permanent +1 from your Aspect (Hunter Muscle, Prey Reflex, Pack Savvy, Den Root), flat and additive on top of species.

active.name: Let It Out
active.text: Take 1 Stress to partly shift for a scene: natural weapons (Light, Blade or Impact by Aspect) and +1 die on tracking, chasing, intimidating, or enduring. Visibly not-quite-human while it lasts.

compulsion.name: Instinct
compulsion.text: Your Aspect's instinct presses harder as Stress rises: Hunter chases what runs, Prey bolts when cornered, Pack will not leave its people, Den will not give up ground. At high Stress the GM may have the Instinct take the first beat of your turn.

weakness.name: Bane
weakness.text: Your bloodline sets your Bane: Silver for Lycans, cold iron for Fae-touched lines, a Crownline or Helix deterrent for lab lines, electrical shock or EMP for Bastion biotech. A Bane hit adds one Wound step; direct contact or sustained exposure ends Let It Out and blocks it until the end of your next turn. Never softens with Evolution.
weakness.deterrentFields: Crownline and Helix also field area deterrents: sonic emitters, frequency fields, scent sprays. While inside one, every Beastkin's animal senses are overwhelmed (no free read; -1 die to notice or track). If the field matches your Bane, you also cannot use Let It Out and take 1 Stress when it switches on or when you enter it.

complication.name: Registered Beastkin
complication.text: ACR wants you on the registry and AEM files you under public health; neither will take responsibility for you. Any animal attack in the district puts your name on a list, and Bastion and Helix both read that list.

progression.Dormant: Senses only; adaptation not online. Instinct is a pull, not a push.
progression.Awakened: Permanent +1 online; Let It Out available.
progression.Integrated: Let It Out is cheaper or longer (pending playtest); Instinct intrudes more under Stress; Bane exposure also costs 1 Stress.
progression.Manifest: Full shift becomes possible (scope TBD); deep Stress can force a Breakdown-like complication; a Bane hit adds two Wound steps.
progression.Ascendant: Capstone shift abilities; under high Stress the GM may direct one action per scene; even brief Bane contact moves the Wound Track.

openQuestions: Do the numbers hold up at the table: Let It Out at 1 Stress, Bane +1 Wound step, deterrent fields at -1 die and 1 Stress?
Should Lycan or any other line be limited to certain Aspects (for example, Lycan only Hunter or Pack)?
What does a full shift at Manifest look like?

lines.name: Lycan
lines.text: The old moon-curse line. The one every Velvet Signal horror stream gets wrong.

lines.name: Fae-touched
lines.text: An ancestor crossed the Fae and the debt came due in the blood. The World Anvil leaves open whether Fae-touched can stand as its own affliction; here it is a Beastkin line.

lines.name: Lab line
lines.text: A great-grandparent was a Helix trial subject, by consent form or without one. Crownline and Helix both keep deterrents tuned for what came out of it.

lines.name: Biotech
lines.text: Spliced, sampled, or patched with Bastion biotech somewhere up the family tree, from the same program that built the retrieval units. Bastion still wants the samples back.

lines.name: Visceral
lines.text: Contamination from the Visceral side of the world, the body refusing ordinary limits. You are still not Slimefolk and not Visceral by lineage. Pick the Bane with your GM.
